content.title: Can you see the Artemis II rocket launch from the Tampa Bay area?
content.text: The first crewed moon mission in more than 50 years could launch as soon as Wednesday evening from Florida's Space Coast. So, what are our chances of catching a glimpse of the Artemis II rocket?Our 10 Tampa Bay News meteorologists agree that conditions look favorable for the first launch window, which opens at 6:24 p.m. on April 1.There's an 80% chance of liftoff for Wednesday evening, but visibility will depend heavily on cloud cover — and where you’re watching from.Cape Canaveral could see gusty winds, increased cloud coverage and the chance of isolated showers in the morning, but it looks like those showers will shift over to the Tampa Bay area for the afternoon and evening.So while weather likely won't interfere with the launch, cloudy conditions could make it difficult for us to see the rocket from the Tampa Bay region.NASA released a visibility range chart for the Artemis II launch, which shows that here in Tampa, St. Pete, Clearwater and Sarasota, we should be able to see the rocket about 40 seconds after liftoff if skies are clear.If you do plan to watch locally, higher vantage points will help. Think rooftops and tall buildings.If you want an even better view, you could take a drive to the Lake Wales, St. Cloud, or Orlando areas, where the clouds should be clear by launch time.The good news is, our crews will be at Kennedy Space Center giving you a front-row seat to the Artemis II launch on the free 10 Tampa Bay News streaming app.Anchor Dave Wagner will be live from the launch site and take you behind the scenes with a retired NASA astronaut to explain why this mission matters so much and why this crew will be flying around the moon, not landing on it.What time is the Artemis II launch?There are a series of potential launch times in April for the Artemis II mission:April 1: 6:24 p.m. – 8:24 p.m. ETApril 2: 7:22 p.m. – 9:22 p.m. ETApril 3: 8:00 p.m. – 10:00 p.m. ETApril 4: 8:53 p.m. – 10:53 p.m. ETApril 5: 9:40 p.m. – 11:40 p.m. ETApril 6: 10:36 p.m. – 12:36 a.m. ETApril 30: 6:06 p.m. – 8:06 p.m. ETTEGNA Digital and the Associated Press contributed to this report.
